modality_tier_compat_note: A (modality, tier) pair whose tier is not in the modality's allowed list is NOT emittable by the deterministic procedure (rubric §C.5) and is rejected at freeze. Forbidden pairs explicitly include shadow-down/E0, emergence-up/E1, and any recognition-landing tier other than E2. Mirrors the rubric §B.8 table. The modality checked against this table is the PRIMARY modality (the existing per-edge 'modality' field, == primary_modality per modality_precedence_rule); secondary_modalities / conditionality_flags are NOT checked against this table and are never counted in the registered null.

modality_precedence_rule.summary: Each edge has EXACTLY ONE primary_modality (the existing 'modality' field; NOT renamed) used for (modality,tier) emittability and headline/registered-null reporting. An edge MAY also carry an OPTIONAL secondary_modalities array and/or conditionality_flags array, which are descriptive residual annotations ONLY and are NEVER used for emittability or counting.
modality_precedence_rule.primary_modality_note: The existing per-edge 'modality' field IS the primary_modality. This rule does NOT rename it. The freeze validator continues to read 'modality' for emittability (modality_tier_compat) and for the registered-null tally; it is the primary_modality.
rule: (1) STRUCTURAL-IS-PRIMARY: if any STRUCTURAL modality test passes -- duality (B.3), common-refinement (B.4), holonomy (B.6), currency-shadow-price (B.5), shadow-down/descent (B.1), or emergence-up (B.2) -- that structural modality is the primary_modality (resolved among themselves by the rubric B.7 precedence chain duality>common-refinement>holonomy>currency>descent>emergence when more than one passes).

(2) RECOGNITION-LANDING-IS-RESIDUAL-PRIMARY: recognition-landing (B.6a) is the primary_modality ONLY when NO structural modality closes the edge AND the imported named principle is the ENTIRE landing mechanism (the B.6a RECOGNITION-ONLY test (i)-(iii) all hold). This is unchanged from B.6a/B.7.

(3) RECOGNITION-CONDITIONAL-IS-A-SECONDARY-FLAG: if a STRUCTURAL modality is primary but the edge is at tier E2 and still requires a NAMED external import to close, record 'recognition-conditional' in conditionality_flags (equivalently secondary_modalities). This is DISTINCT from primary recognition-landing: the structural test passed (so the edge is NOT residual), but its E2 closure is conditional on a named import. The primary modality stays structural; the secondary flag records the import conditionality.
modality_precedence_rule.discriminator: Primary recognition-landing requires NO structural test passes (B.6a (i)-(iii)); a recognition-conditional SECONDARY flag is used precisely when a structural test DID pass but the edge nevertheless lands E2 via a named import. The two are mutually exclusive on a given edge: an edge is EITHER primary recognition-landing (residual) OR a structural primary carrying a recognition-conditional secondary flag, never both.
modality_precedence_rule.currency_exemplar_crossref: The structural relation for E005 is the rubric B.5 currency/shadow-price exemplar 'surface gravity as the price in black-hole thermodynamics' (TYPING_RUBRIC.md B.5). Because that structural test passes, E005's primary_modality is currency-shadow-price, NOT recognition-landing.

secondary_modalities.meaning: OPTIONAL descriptive residual annotation(s) on an edge whose primary_modality is structural. Currently the only defined secondary value is 'recognition-conditional' (a structural E2 edge whose closure leans on a named import). NEVER used for emittability (modality_tier_compat) and NEVER counted in the registered_null. NOTE: 'recognition-conditional' is a SECONDARY-FLAG string and is intentionally NOT a member of canonical_modalities (which are the PRIMARY-modality strings); it may appear ONLY in secondary_modalities/conditionality_flags, never as the primary 'modality' field.

conditionality_flags.meaning: Equivalent carrier for conditionality annotations (e.g. ['recognition-conditional']); an edge may use conditionality_flags and/or secondary_modalities to record that its E2 structural closure is conditional on a named import.

recognition_resolution.decision_summary: RESOLVED R2 by ADDING 'recognition-landing' as an explicit canonical modality (rubric §B.6a) rather than retagging. The recognition-landing edges span both arrow directions (up and down) and different underlying mechanisms (failed descent, top-down currency, located emergence); a retag map would scatter them across descent/currency/emergence and ERASE the single fact that defines them. Recognition-landing is tier-locked to E2.
recognition_resolution.operational_test: An edge is a recognition-landing iff ALL THREE hold on the declared toy model M: (i) no internal descent closes it (descent-test fails, Xi != 0 stably); (ii) no internal duality (B.3) and no internal common-refinement (B.4) closes it; (iii) the edge is characterized ONLY by a single named, citable external principle imported under a stated closure assumption (remove the named import and no inter-layer relation remains). If any structural test passes, the edge is that structural modality, NOT a recognition-landing. If recognition-search returns nothing named, it is NOT a recognition-landing but a sharpened gap E3, re-typed by its arrow before sealing.
recognition_resolution.membership_rule: MEMBERSHIP IS RULE-DRIVEN, NOT A HARD COUNT (R2): the affected_edges set is DEFINED as 'every edge row in edge_manifest.jsonl whose audited modality == recognition-landing'. The validator enumerates recognition-landing rows from the manifest and asserts the set equals affected_edges below; it does NOT trust a frozen integer. affected_edges is the frozen enumeration of that set at this freeze (currently 8 rows). If the manifest's recognition-landing set changes, affected_edges must be re-enumerated to match -- a stale list is rejected.

split_type_meaning.form_value: the FORM of a relation descends/lands at form_tier (typically E1) while its NUMERICAL VALUES are run-only or imported (value_tier in {E0, E2})
split_type_meaning.form_value_imported: sub-case of form_value: geometry/form descends (E1) but the predictive CONTENT is an imported named principle (value_tier E2)
split_type_meaning.theorem_run: the analytic OPEN-THEOREM status is form_tier E3 (open named external problem) while the RUN-EXHIBITED phenomenon is value_tier E0 (a substrate run exhibits it)

reported_tier_rule.rule: reported_tier is SPLIT-TYPE-DEPENDENT (not a flat form_tier). It names which leg carries the edge's PRIMARY (headline) claim, which is the leg counted in the registered null; the OTHER leg is recorded on a separate ledger and NEVER summed.
reported_tier_rule.rationale_form_value: for split_type in {form_value, form_value_imported} the edge's PRIMARY claim is the PREDICTIVE inter-layer connection, which is incomplete without the imported/run-generated value leg (e.g. ChPT is not predictive from the symmetry skeleton alone; it needs the run-generated LECs). The headline tier is therefore the value_tier; the form-descends leg is recorded but is NOT the edge's claimed closure status. CONSEQUENCE (R3 SINGLE SEMANTICS): E029 (ChPT) has form_tier E1 / value_tier E2 / split_type form_value_imported, so its reported (headline) tier is the value_tier E2 (recognition-conditional on the imported run-generated LECs). The headline (edge_scored_tier) EQUALS reported_tier=E2 -- the strong headline_tier_invariant with no nuance exception. The form-descends-E1 leg is recorded but is NOT counted in the E1 null; the two legs are never summed. (E029 does not contribute to the E1 count.)
reported_tier_rule.rationale_theorem_run: for split_type == theorem_run the edge's PRIMARY claim is the ANALYTIC THEOREM status (the open named external problem); the run-exhibited leg is a SEPARATE never-summed E0 ledger entry. The headline tier is therefore the form_tier. CONSEQUENCE: E041 (confinement) has form_tier E3 / value_tier E0 / split_type theorem_run, so its reported (headline) tier STAYS E3; the lattice-run-exhibited string tension is the E0 ledger leg, carried separately, never summed.
reported_tier_rule.headline_tier_invariant: A row's headline (scored) tier MUST EQUAL value_split.reported_tier (the value computed by reported_tier_by_split_type for that row's split_type). A row whose scored_tier disagrees with its value_split.reported_tier is rejected at freeze (validator check C10). Under the R3 single semantics this is exact for E029: split_type form_value_imported => reported_tier = value_tier = E2 = edge_scored_tier (no nuance exception). For the form_value descent rows E004/E008/E035a/E038 the reported leg is the value_tier (E0, the run-only numerical values carried separately on the Run-Target ledger), while the edge's own closure is the EQUATION/STRUCTURE descent E1 fixed by calibration/descent; here the edge_scored_tier (E1) is the edge's audited closure and the E0 value-leg is a SEPARATE never-summed Run-Target entry, neither counted in the E1 null as the value leg. The narrow invariant the validator enforces (C10): scored_tier may equal the contract's frozen per-row edge_scored_tier, but it must NOT be silently set to a value_split leg that the reported_tier_rule says is NOT the reported leg (it must not report the form_tier of a form_value row as if that form-leg were the edge's predictive closure).

value_split_schema.no_summing_within_edge: the NON-reported leg is carried SEPARATELY (into the Run-Target Manifest when E0, the conditional ledger when E2) and is NEVER summed with the reported_tier leg, independent of split_type. For form_value/form_value_imported the reported leg is the value_tier and the form_tier (E1) leg is NOT counted in the E1 null; for theorem_run the reported leg is the form_tier (E3) and the run-exhibited value_tier (E0) leg is the separate ledger entry.

near_intra_layer_check.meaning: true iff this edge is subject to the near-intra-layer gate E.4/E.11 (it is a candidate within-a-layer restriction that MUST pass the E.4 relabeling test before it may count as a clean E1). The legacy free-text 'PENDING_E4: ...' string is superseded by this boolean plus near_intra_layer_result; the prose remains as a human note but the validator reads these two machine fields.

near_intra_layer_result.meaning: pending = E.4 relabeling test not yet run/recorded (the v3 state for E016/E017/E039); passed = E.4 confirmed a GENUINE inter-layer quotient (own Sigma_f, own accepted_observables; removing the renaming leaves a residual relation) -> the edge MAY be a sealed E1; failed = E.4 showed a within-layer tensor-factor restriction (removing the renaming leaves no residual relation) -> the edge is 'within-a-layer, no SBT content', REMOVED from the E1 count.

near_intra_layer_schema.rule: scored_tier E1 is FORBIDDEN for a near_intra_layer_check:true edge UNLESS near_intra_layer_result == 'passed'. A pending result means the edge may be carried only as 'E1-pending', never counted as a sealed E1. A failed gate-E.4 (near_intra_layer_result == 'failed') => the edge is REMOVED from the E1 count and marked 'within-a-layer, no SBT content' (its modality/tier no longer contributes E1).
near_intra_layer_schema.validator_assertion: in scored mode, for every edge with near_intra_layer_check == true and scored_tier == 'E1', assert near_intra_layer_result == 'passed'; otherwise reject. (A scored copy that sets every scored_tier=provisional but leaves E016/E017/E039 as unresolved E1 must FAIL here -- the reviewer's mutation test 1.)
near_intra_layer_schema.current_state: E016, E017, E039 all carry near_intra_layer_check:true, near_intra_layer_result:'pending' at this freeze (E.4 not yet run); none may be counted as a sealed E1.

tier_order_meaning: the single conservatism/informativeness ordering E1 (most-flattering) > E2 > E0 > E3 (least-flattering); E3 is the unique conservative terminal; doubt demotes strictly toward E3; E0 is NOT a doubt-haven (sealing it needs the positive construction of a non-descending run-object, gate E.7). rubric §E.5.
no_summing_full: The four tiers live on separate ledgers and are reported per tier, never pooled. E2 (recognition-conditional) and E0 (run-only, deferred) are never summed with E1 (accepted descent). Even WITHIN a single edge, a value_split's value_tier is never summed with its form_tier (independent of split_type).

normalized_xi_criterion.review_fix: R-P2 (Pause-2: the descent test reads the NORMALIZED relative residual, not the raw Xi norm)
normalized_xi_criterion.provenance: EXTERNAL_REVIEW_PAUSE2.md OTHER FINDINGS (E001: raw Xi grows 7.84e8->2.25e9 but the relative residual shrinks 0.197->0.042 while staying positive; base the E0-vs-E1 descent criterion on the NORMALIZED residual).
normalized_xi_criterion.definition: the relative residual xi_rel(h) := ||Xi_C(D|L; h)|| / ||K_DD(h)||, a dimensionless ratio in [0,1] -- the located obstruction normalized by the total source-readout currency K_DD (the fraction of the dissolving readout T_D lying outside the native range P_L). xi_rel = 0 <=> Xi = 0 (exact-adequacy equivalence preserved), but xi_rel is SCALE-INVARIANT and is the quantity the descent test reads.
normalized_xi_criterion.report_both: the edge log MUST report BOTH the raw Xi and the normalized xi_rel at EACH of the two refinements h1, h2; the descent verdict is taken from xi_rel, NEVER from the raw Xi norm alone (a small raw Xi is NOT sufficient for E1; a large/growing raw Xi is NOT disqualifying).
normalized_xi_criterion.E1_criterion: CLEAN DESCENT (E1) requires xi_rel -> ~machine-zero STABLY across both declared refinements h1 ⊏ h2 (gate E.9), AND no-over-read (E.3). The refinement-stability check (E.9) is on xi_rel, not raw Xi.
normalized_xi_criterion.E0_E3_criterion: E0/E3 (obstruction / gap): the NORMALIZED residual stays BOUNDED AWAY FROM ZERO under refinement (a stable positive relative residual) WITH ANALYTIC CONTROL of that fraction (a known nonzero lower bound, not a numerical accident). This is the normalized analogue of Xi > 0.
normalized_xi_criterion.worked_example_E001: E001 (QCD -> hadron-spectrum, the E0 anchor) is the canonical STABLE-POSITIVE-NORMALIZED-RESIDUAL + ANALYTIC-CONTROL example: raw Xi GROWS (7.84e8 -> 2.25e9) under refinement but the NORMALIZED residual shrinks toward a stable positive floor (xi_rel 0.197 -> 0.042) and STAYS POSITIVE -- it does NOT reach machine-zero. The E0/E3 signal is exactly this (stable positive normalized residual + analytic control), NOT monotone raw growth. The proton mass is run-only (no D0=A.L0 shortcut); the positive xi_rel floor is the blind-spot currency of the missing run. Hence E001 seals E0 (its modality is emergence; rubric C.4).
normalized_xi_criterion.worked_example_E005: E005 (GR -> black-hole-thermodynamics) is the canonical OVER-READ example: classical GR's toy-model Xi comes out NUMERICALLY SMALL (xi_rel ~ 0 on a GR-only probe family) -- but this is an OVER-READ (gate E.3 fail), NOT a clean descent. The h-bar coefficients and the thermal reinterpretation (T = kappa/2pi, S = A/4) are NOT in GR's Sigma_f, so a GR-only probe family literally cannot express the thermal predicates; its small Xi certifies adequacy only for the NON-thermal content and silently drops the imported h-bar/thermal predicates. Once the thermal observables are in the readout map (D.4.v) the descent over-reads its source (E.3) and is blocked; the edge lands E2 via the named import. Lesson: a small numeric Xi when h-bar/thermal predicates are imported is an OVER-READ, not an E1.
normalized_xi_criterion.rubric_ref: TYPING_RUBRIC.md D.1.1, C.1, C.5 STEP 1, E.9

gate_policy.review_fix: R-P2 (Pause-2: the calibration gate-policy adjudicated by the external reviewer)
gate_policy.provenance: EXTERNAL_REVIEW_PAUSE2.md Gate policy + Adjudication (tier-only hard for calibration; modality mismatch routed to adjudication, not auto-fail).
gate_policy.calibration_hard_gate: TIER ONLY. Calibration PASS/FAIL hard-gates on the per-row TIER: every is_calibration must_seal_* row's computed_tier must EQUAL its calibration_known_tier, and every must_not_seal_E1_or_E2 anti-control's computed_tier must land in {E3, E0} (E0 only with the E.7 interlock). A tier mismatch on a calibration row BLOCKS the freeze.
gate_policy.modality_hard_checks: modality checks hard-gate on: (i) canonical modality strings (canonical_modalities; every PRIMARY modality string is one of the 7); (ii) primary-modality/tier emittability (modality_tier_compat, on the PRIMARY modality); (iii) recognition-import hygiene (C11 for primary recognition-landing rows AND C13 for secondary recognition-conditional flags). These are hard freeze-blockers.
gate_policy.modality_mismatch_is_adjudicated_not_aut: A blind-vs-frozen PRIMARY-modality MISMATCH on a calibration row is ROUTED TO ADJUDICATION (recorded, then the scored gate re-run on the adjudicated modality), NOT auto-failed. Rationale (reviewer): modality is empirically LESS deterministic than tier on hard/faceted edges -- two of nine Pause-2 blind edges (E005, E018) disagreed on modality while getting tier right. The tier gate is the hard calibration gate; the modality is adjudicated. (E005: blind currency vs frozen currency-shadow-price -- now resolved primary currency-shadow-price + secondary recognition-conditional. E018: blind emergence-up vs frozen common-refinement, tier E3 either way.)
gate_policy.do_not_force_align_silently: When a blind run disagrees with the frozen primary modality, the adjudication MUST be recorded (not silently force-aligned) and the scored gate re-run; the resolution and the re-run are logged.
gate_policy.freeze_notes_ref: recorded in FREEZE_NOTES.md (gate-policy section) and enforced via the freeze_gate_predicate clauses (c) [canonical+emittable] and (g)/(h) [C11/C13 import hygiene].
